subject: Bond has a face, and Monday had other plans
summary: Amazon MGM named its next James Bond, New York is breaking up a police unit, and Detroit lost its pass rusher again.

lead.head: Robert Pattinson is the next Bond
text: The casting rumour mill is done, and Amazon MGM ended it the way modern studios do: with a video on its own account. Robert Pattinson is the next James Bond. Denis Villeneuve will direct.

Look at where the attention went. The official Bond account carried the announcement and its origin post, and between them they drew most of the day's reach on this story. DiscussingFilm, a film news account, added a third post on top. Nobody had to chase a leak, because the studio held the microphone itself.
That is the point of a months-long guessing game. The rumours were free advertising, and the announcement collects the payoff on a day the studio picks.

notes.head: New York will disband a police unit
notes.text: The mayor of New York City says he is disbanding the NYPD's Strategic Response Group. The unit handled both protests and counterterrorism, and the plan splits those two jobs between other hands. Supporters and critics describe that split in opposite ways. Representative Nancy Mace was among the voices who weighed in.

notes.head: Lions lose Hutchinson to a torn ACL
notes.text: NFL Network reports Aidan Hutchinson is out for the season with a torn ACL, hurt celebrating a sack in Munich on Sunday. It is the second time in three years an injury has ended his season. Separately, NFL Network reports Patriots quarterback Drake Maye was hurt in the same city and may miss the rest of the year, and ESPN reports the team fears a fractured ankle.

notes.head: Big banks had a bad Monday afternoon
notes.text: Customers of several large US banks could not log in, see balances or move money on Monday afternoon. Chase calls it a technical issue and says it is not a cyber issue. That is the company's account of the cause, and the posts that spread the news do not add a confirmed one.

text: The day was mostly about who controls the announcement. A studio picked its moment and got the biggest reach of the day. A mayor picked his and left everyone arguing over what the change means. A bank had no say at all, and could only call it technical.

My call is that the controlled news is the least important of the three. A new Bond is a fine story, but a police unit being split in two and payments failing for an afternoon are the ones that change how people live.
